title: A devilish masterpiece
gist: Sukhdev Sandhu reappraises Ken Russell, a once-celebrated director who drifted to the margins, as a new 4K restoration of his notorious 1971 film The Devils returns to cinemas with cut footage restored. He argues the blasphemy charge was silly and that the film depicts how politicians can weaponise religion.

insights.claim: Ken Russell, who died aged 84 in 2011, had become an almost forgotten director in Britain despite early acclaim, including a description as 'perhaps the greatest TV director of all time'.
insights.speaker: Sukhdev Sandhu
insights.so_what: Illustrates how reputational cycles can revive the value of neglected creative catalogues.

insights.claim: Russell's 1969 Women in Love was nominated for four Academy Awards and won Glenda Jackson the best actress Oscar.
insights.speaker: Sukhdev Sandhu
insights.so_what: Context on the commercial peak of Russell's catalogue.

insights.claim: Russell was often attacked as baroque and vulgar; Dance of the Seven Veils was shown only once by the BBC and provoked 20 Conservative MPs to denounce it in a parliamentary motion.
insights.speaker: Sukhdev Sandhu
insights.so_what: Shows historical censorship and political backlash against provocative content.

insights.claim: The Devils (1971), adapted from Aldous Huxley about the 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, had its 'Rape of Christ' sequence cut before release, was cut further in the US, and was banned by several local councils and some countries.
insights.speaker: Sukhdev Sandhu
insights.so_what: Censored-then-restored works can be re-released as premium cultural events.

insights.claim: A new 4K restoration of The Devils, returning the cut footage, is being released in cinemas, showcasing Derek Jarman's set design, Peter Maxwell Davies's score and David Watkin's cinematography.
insights.speaker: Sukhdev Sandhu
insights.so_what: Part of a broader trend of restored-classic theatrical releases.

insights.claim: Sandhu argues the blasphemy charge against The Devils is silly because Russell was a Catholic convert whose early shorts were backed by the Catholic Film Institute.
insights.speaker: Sukhdev Sandhu
insights.so_what: Reframes a controversial work, supporting its critical rehabilitation.
insights.quote: The charge of blasphemy often levelled at the film is silly.

insights.claim: Sandhu reads The Devils as an image of how politicians can weaponise religion and how quickly civil society can be turned into rubble.
insights.speaker: Sukhdev Sandhu
insights.so_what: Explains the film's renewed contemporary resonance.
